findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No certified food protection manager (CFPM) was available during the inspection. The inspector advised the person-in-charge (PIC) to get certified in food protection management so that a CFPM is available during all hours of food preparation/operation. The director of the program is certified but shares some time with Nokomis schools. See that more than one person is certified within the facility. Operator present during the inspection has a certificate that just expired on March 2. She intends to retake the course and test sometime within the next week.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. The facility dish machine operator had no knowledge of testing the heat sanitizing dish machine using a maximum registering thermometer. An image of the device was shared with the dish operator. See that the facility purchases and uses (daily) the thermometer to insure the accuracy of the dish machine. Operator knew to check the display to ensure the rinse temperature was at least 180F.
(A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [PF]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. No food handler cards were available for present staff. Only one employee was recently hired. See that all staff are either certified food managers or food handlers as required. There should be one certified food managers present during all hours of operations. Anyone else should have the food handlers card. 

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect food from exposure to potential contaminants.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed that the facility has Quat and Lactic Acid test strips available but they use Chlorine sanitizer (bleach). The inspector had an extra package of Chlorine test strips which were provided to the facility during the inspection. The PIC will be purchasing more of the correct test strips as well. Ensure test kits are always available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions.
